Integration of cross cutting, electrically-powered, volumetric drying process intensification technologies based on Radio Frequency (RF) and acoustics (Ultrasonics) (US) will directly impart energy into the biomaterials resulting in improved energy efficiency and throughput. Integration of RFUS-based drying technology is expected to enable U.S. manufacturing industry to reduce capital and operating costs, energy consumption, and carbon emissions while increasing energy efficiency and throughput, improving product quality and sustainability, and helping preserve U.S. manufacturing jobs. The hybrid drying approach incorporates directed radio frequency (RF) and ultrasonic (US) energy with conventional conduction, diffusion and convective heat and mass transfer overcoming the limitations of the conventional drying processes and that meets/exceeds the minimum goals. We have shown the effective removal of free and bound water in the biomaterials by leveraging the synergies of RF and US technologies integrated with conventional manufacturing processes. An experimental setup capable of monitoring and capturing instantaneous drying characteristics with high resolutions was developed to accurately study the alternating conductive and convective drying of paper and board. Experimental investigation of the integration of RF and US energies at varying drying times and sheet moisture conditions during alternating conduction and convection drying (i.e., duplicating commercial multi-cylinder drying) has also been evaluated. Integrating RF drying is indeed an effective method for paper drying applications with greater improvements in drying rates and energy intensities at higher moisture contents. US applications in the pockets (along with convection or pocket ventilation systems) after conduction on the cylinders are more favorable resulting in reasonable improvements in drying rate and energy intensity for all basis weights studied. With optimal integration of RFUS technology we were able to alter the drying rate profile and improve the overall drying performance. Results clearly showed that with optimum integration of RFUS at various locations/sheet moisture contents on the paper machine, the desired target improvements in drying rate and drying time can be reached, thus achieving the project goals (30% increase in drying rate and production/throughput rate). Based on techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle analysis (LCA) of commercial paper machine drying sections and experimental and modeling results, the necessary process and operating conditions and mix of energy inputs were determined to achieve the targeted 20% reduction in energy intensity and 25% reduction in carbon intensity. As part of this work, we have evaluated the feasibility of integrating the RFUS technology with manufacturing three major packaging grades, namely linerboard, corrugating medium and bleached board.
